prompt.context_jp: 重役の並ぶ会議室で、最後の意思確認が交わされようとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その席には社長の井手美香もみずから出席し、緊張した空気___テーブルの上を静かに流れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits this narrative description.

feedback.correct_en: The tense atmosphere is newly introduced information describing the scene — が marks this fresh, observable state rather than a topic the narrator and reader already share.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make '緊張した空気' a topic already under discussion, but here it's being introduced as new scenic information.

prompt.context_jp: 営業事業部への案内が始まれば…
prompt.prompt_jp: そこにいるはずの新入社員・井手裕太郎の不在___隠しきれず、たちどころに露見してしまう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the appropriate particle.

feedback.correct_en: The absence is the topic being commented on — the narrator tells us what will happen to it. は frames '不在' as the known subject under discussion.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the absence as brand-new information, but the sentence is predicating something about an already-established concern.

prompt.context_jp: 里中が東海林に緊急事態を告げる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「裕太郎君___ いなくなったみたい」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this urgent report?

feedback.correct_en: This is breaking news to Tokairin — が marks Yutaro as newly-introduced information in an unexpected event report.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Yutaro is already the topic of conversation, but Satonaka is announcing the disappearance as fresh urgent news.

prompt.context_jp: 裕太郎が消えた直後、さらに…
prompt.prompt_jp: 「大前さん___行方不明みたい」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits adding another missing person to the situation?

feedback.correct_en: The story uses も here — adding Omae to the already-established fact that Yutaro is missing. 'Also missing' is the natural meaning.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Omae as new unrelated information; は would isolate her as a contrasted topic. も captures 'in addition to Yutaro.'

prompt.context_jp: 一方その頃、
prompt.prompt_jp: 井手裕太郎___社屋の地下深く、業務用の巨大な冷凍庫のなかにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits a scene-shift narrative sentence?

feedback.correct_en: '一方その頃' signals a topic shift — は re-establishes Yutaro as the topic for this new scene, telling us where he is.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Yutaro as brand-new information, but he's an already-known character; the sentence predicates his location.

contrast_examples.en: Meanwhile, Taro was at home. (topic shift)

contrast_examples.jp: ドアの前に太郎がいた。
contrast_examples.en: Taro was in front of the door. (new observation)

prompt.context_jp: 大前が冷凍庫でスマホが切れた理由を説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ここの気温___0.6度」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits when stating a fact about the current place?

feedback.correct_en: 'ここの気温' is the topic — she's telling him *about* the temperature here. は presents it as the subject being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like she's suddenly reporting a new discovery; she's calmly explaining the known condition of the freezer.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が叫んでも無駄だと説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そこの扉___厚いんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the right particle.

feedback.correct_en: She's describing a property of a specific known object (that door) — は marks it as the topic she's commenting on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the door as new or exhaustively list it; here she's simply characterizing an already-visible object.

contrast_examples.en: This wall is thick. (describing known object)

contrast_examples.jp: 壁が厚くて声が届かない。
contrast_examples.en: The wall is thick, so voices don't reach. (reason/subordinate)

prompt.context_jp: 大前が派遣の厳しさを語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「派遣___休んだら 食べていけません」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits a contrastive generalization about a group?

feedback.correct_en: She contrasts temps (派遣) with salaried employees — は marks '派遣' as the topic/contrasted category being characterized.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a one-off new subject; her point is a general truth contrasting temps vs. employees.

contrast_examples.jp: 社員は守られています。

prompt.context_jp: 大前は自分の時給の高さを強調する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私のお時給___ とても高いんです！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this emphatic declaration?

feedback.correct_en: '私のお時給' is being presented as the topic she's boasting about; は frames it as the subject under comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a sudden new observation, but she's declaring a known fact about her value with topical emphasis.

contrast_examples.en: My hourly wage is high. (asserting about known topic)
Oh, my wage went up! (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 最後の一節を叩き終えたその瞬間、
prompt.prompt_jp: 遠くから足音___近づいてきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits a sudden perceivable event.

feedback.correct_en: Footsteps appearing is a newly-perceived event — が marks '足音' as fresh, observable information arriving into the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply footsteps were an already-known topic; the drama here is their sudden appearance.

prompt.context_jp: 時間稼ぎのプレゼン中。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林の脱線___とどまるところを知らなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the appropriate particle.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is commenting on Tokairin's digressions as an established ongoing thing — は marks it as the topic being evaluated.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the digressions as newly-noticed information, but by this point they are the running theme.

contrast_examples.en: His stories are long. (characterizing a topic)

prompt.context_jp: 息子が無事に戻ってきた場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 井手美香___しばらく息子の顔を見つめてから、ようやく安堵の表情を浮かべた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this narrative?

feedback.correct_en: Ide Mika is an already-known character; は marks her as the topic whose actions and feelings are being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as new, but she's been present in the scene — the narrator is telling us what she does.

contrast_examples.jp: ある女性が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 母としての感情が溢れる瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の目にはいつのまにか涙___にじんでいたが、そこは社長らしく、すぐに笑顔で覆い隠された。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the appropriate particle.

feedback.correct_en: Tears welling up is a newly-emerging phenomenon — が marks '涙' as new information noticed within the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make tears the topic (as if contrasting with something else); here they simply appear as a fresh detail.

contrast_examples.en: Tears welled up in her eyes. (new emergence)
Those tears were unexpected. (referring back to known tears)

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の就任朝礼の場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最前列には、派遣として席を占める大前春子の姿___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits an existential scene-setting description.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence presents what exists at the front row — a classic 'there was X' structure uses が to introduce the new element in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 大前春子の姿 as a pre-established topic, but here the narrative is pointing out/introducing her presence.

contrast_examples.en: There was a cat in the garden. (existential new info)

prompt.context_jp: 大前が裕太郎に冷たく告げる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「正社員も 満足に務まらない人に 派遣___務まりません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle to complete this contrastive judgment.

feedback.correct_en: She's contrasting 正社員 with 派遣 — は marks '派遣' as the contrasted category: 'if even that, then as for temp work, no way.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply name the subject neutrally and lose the contrastive bite that makes her put-down sting.

contrast_examples.jp: 社員もだめ、派遣はもっとだめ。

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が自分の立場を訴える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「俺だって やっと つかんだ チャンス___なんだから」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before なんだから here?

feedback.correct_en: The phrase 'チャンスなんだから' uses the copula な+んだから to assert 'it IS a chance' — no case particle needed.
feedback.incorrect_en: を/が would be case markers for objects/subjects, but here チャンス is a predicate nominal joined to the copula.

contrast_examples.jp: これはチャンスなんだ。

prompt.context_jp: 裕太郎が扉を叩いて叫ぶ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は分厚い金属扉に取りついて、力任せに拳___叩きつけ、声を限りに助けを呼んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what he strikes.

feedback.correct_en: 拳 is the direct object of 叩きつけ (to slam) — を marks what is being struck/slammed.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination; が would mark subject. 叩きつける takes を for the thing being slammed.

contrast_examples.en: Slam one's fist against the wall.

prompt.context_jp: 気取られぬよう緊急に合図する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中は宮部たちに気取られぬよう、東海林の袖___強く引いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Satonaka pulls.

feedback.correct_en: 袖 is the direct object of 引く (to pull) — を marks what's being pulled.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark direction/target; が would mark subject. 'Pull the sleeve' takes を.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が商談相手を持ち上げる台詞。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今や ___勢いの テイスト･オブ･ライフさんの お眼鏡にかないまして…」
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase describes a company's unstoppable momentum?

feedback.correct_en: 飛ぶ鳥を落とす勢い means 'momentum so great it could knock a bird out of the sky' — a stock business compliment for a thriving company.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水を得た魚 describes someone in their element; 猫の手も借りたい means being extremely busy. Neither fits 'unstoppable company momentum.'

contrast_examples.jp: 飛ぶ鳥を落とす勢いの新興企業。
水を得た魚のように働く。
contrast_examples.en: Work like a fish in water.

prompt.context_jp: 商談が成立した喜びを表す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「テイスト･オブ･ライフさんの ___ 私のビスコッティも 大変光栄でございます」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the business idiom meaning 'to meet with approval'.

choices.text: お眼鏡にかないまして

feedback.correct_en: お眼鏡にかなう means 'to meet someone's approval / pass their discerning judgment' — exactly what Tokairin claims his product did.
feedback.incorrect_en: お耳に入れる means 'to inform someone'; お手を煩わせる means 'to trouble someone.' Neither matches 'being approved of.'

contrast_examples.jp: 社長のお眼鏡にかなった。
ご耳に入れておきます。

prompt.context_jp: 里中が東海林に頼み込む。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「東海林さん 何とか 時間 ___ くれないかな」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 時間 to mean 'buy time / stall'?

feedback.correct_en: 時間を稼ぐ is the fixed expression for 'buy time / stall' — exactly what Satonaka needs Tokairin to do.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時間を伸ばす isn't a natural collocation; 時間を作る means 'make time (for someone)' which has a different nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 契約の重要性を述べる。
prompt.prompt_jp: ここで場を持たせ切れなければすべてが___に帰す。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'come to nothing'.

feedback.correct_en: 水泡に帰す ('turn to foam') is the set expression meaning 'all efforts come to naught.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 白紙に戻す means 'return to a blank slate / start over' (different verb). 空気に帰す isn't an idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 大前の冷ややかな答え。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ことに 資格も何もありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits Omae's philosophy about survival.

feedback.correct_en: 生き延びる means 'to survive, to make it through alive' — fitting the freezer-trapped crisis.
feedback.incorrect_en: 生き返る means 'come back to life' (revive); 生き生き means 'lively' — neither captures surviving a crisis.

contrast_examples.jp: 厳しい冬を生き延びる。

prompt.context_jp: 裕太郎が自分の夢を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「もっと広い世界で ___たいんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that matches the idealistic image of spreading one's wings.

feedback.correct_en: 羽ばたく ('flap wings / soar') is the clichéd expression for a young person wanting to leave the nest — the narrator even comments on it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 飛び降りる means 'jump down' (dangerous); 駆け抜ける means 'run through' — neither matches the 'spread my wings' metaphor.

contrast_examples.en: Spread one's wings to the world.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の脱線の粘り強さを評する。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___も積もれば山となるとはこのことか、と里中は感嘆に近い呆れをもって聞いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this famous proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') is the standard proverb about small things accumulating.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 and 水 aren't used in this fixed proverb form, even though they share the 'accumulation' idea.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.

prompt.context_jp: 裕太郎に「生きざま似てますね?」と言われた大前の返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___でもらえますか」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that captures Omae's cold rebuff.

feedback.correct_en: ふざけないでもらえますか ('would you kindly not joke around') is a sharp, polite-sounding rejection — perfect for Omae's deadpan dismissal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 遠慮しないで = 'don't hold back' (invites action); 気にしないで = 'don't worry' — both would reverse the intended put-down.

contrast_examples.jp: ふざけないでください。
遠慮しないでください。

prompt.context_jp: 商談成立の喜びを東海林が表現する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as formal business gratitude?

choices.text: 大変光栄でございます
光栄だと思っています

feedback.correct_en: 大変光栄でございます uses the humble copula ございます with the intensifier 大変 — the register expected in a high-stakes executive meeting.
feedback.incorrect_en: すごく光栄です is too casual for a boardroom; 光栄だと思っています sounds detached and bureaucratic rather than warmly polite.

contrast_examples.jp: 大変光栄でございます。

prompt.context_jp: 5時になった瞬間、大前が退社を告げる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most like Omae's crisp professional exit?

choices.text: 5時でございますので 帰らせていただきたいと思います

feedback.correct_en: Clean, polite, and clipped — 失礼します fits Omae's professional-but-firm style, stating the reason (5時なので) without apology.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual plain speech unsuitable for the workplace; C is over-polite and hedged, the opposite of Omae's decisive tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間なので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: It's time, so excuse me. (polite, decisive)

prompt.context_jp: 大前が裕太郎の『羽ばたきたい』を受け流す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which response best captures Omae's dry, task-focused dismissal?

choices.text: ここを脱出したら 思う存分 羽ばたいてください
それは素敵な夢ですね 応援します
羽ばたけるといいですね がんばって

feedback.correct_en: Omae's style is to deadpan-echo the speaker's own melodramatic word (羽ばたく) while redirecting to the immediate crisis (脱出したら). It sounds polite but cuts.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is sincere encouragement (not her); C is softer and sympathetic. Both lose the ironic, task-first bite that defines Omae.

contrast_examples.jp: 終わってから好きにしてください。
contrast_examples.en: Do as you like after we're done. (dry redirect)

prompt.context_jp: 時間稼ぎのために開発秘話を切り出す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing matches the overly-formal sales-pitch register Tokairin uses?

choices.text: こちらの商品の開発秘話を 披露いたしたく存じます
この商品の開発の話をしたいです
商品のことちょっと話させてもらいます

feedback.correct_en: 披露いたしたく存じます stacks humble verbs (いたす + 存じる) — the elaborate keigo Tokairin lays on to flatter and to buy time.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is plain polite without the ceremonious flavor; C is casual-polite and would sound disrespectful to the client president.

contrast_examples.jp: ご説明いたしたく存じます。
contrast_examples.en: I would like to humbly explain.

prompt.context_jp: 救出直後の大前の最初の要求。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Omae's characteristic no-nonsense priority after escape?

choices.text: ありがとうございました 助かりました
お水を一杯いただけますか

feedback.correct_en: The absurd comedic beat is that Omae, barely recovered, immediately demands receipts — the clipped imperative 出して fits her all-business temperament.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is a normal gratitude expected of a rescued person; C is a reasonable comfort request. Both would break Omae's iconic '時給ロボット' persona.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれてありがとう。
